gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE downscales 4K to 1080p at the receiver end so 4K and 1080p TVs can share one kit, and that it runs 4K60 to 196 ft over Cat5e, while OREI's own pages for both cited OREI kits list one EDID setting for every output, mention no scaler and call for Cat6 or better.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI support articles (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K). Both give an EDID dial or DIP table that sets one format for the whole kit (1080p up to 4K60 4:4:4 HDR, or copy from the loop-out or a CAT/HDBT output). Neither mentions downscaling or says what happens when a 1080p TV and a 4K TV are connected. Both name CAT6/CAT6a/CAT7 cable only. They already cover the no-network-switch rule, one-way PoC and the lack of 4K120, so those are not new. No result covers the J-Tech kit, which ChatGPT showed as 'Best overall 1×4'.
decides: If the shopper is mixing a 4K TV with an older 1080p TV, or reusing Cat5e already in the walls, the J-Tech JTECH-14EX60-AE is the pick among the three ChatGPT showed. J-Tech says it scales 4K down to 1080p at the receiver and runs 4K60 over Cat5e/6. On the OREI kits, a mixed setup means choosing one EDID setting for every screen, either all 1080p or a 4K signal the 1080p set may not take. OREI also names only CAT6/6a/7 cable. If every TV is 4K60 and there is new Cat6, the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K is still the long-run choice (394 ft at 4K60 over HDBaseT). One catch: J-Tech's own store listed the JTECH-14EX60-AE at $302.49 with available=false on 2026-11-10.

findings.label: EDID handling across four HDBaseT receivers
findings.value: One EDID DIP or RS-232 setting for all outputs (1080p up to 4K60 4:4:4 HDR, or copy from LOOP OUT or HDBT OUT 1-4). No scaler or downscaling is mentioned.
findings.source_title: UHD14-EXB400-K Overview and Use Cases – OREI
findings.note: Reach is 394 ft (120 m) at 4K60 and 492 ft (150 m) at 1080p60 over CAT6/6a/7. No network switches. Patch panels are allowed but 'may reduce distance'. The article covers only the four included receivers and says nothing about third-party HDBaseT receivers.

findings.label: How OREI splitters with a scaler handle mixed 4K/1080p screens
findings.value: OREI splitters that do scale compare display EDIDs and may drop every output to the lowest common format. Its BK-102A FAQ gives the example of a 4K HDR TV and a 1080p SDR TV both getting 1080p SDR. Its TV-EDID-mode splitters downscale only the 1080p outputs when OUT 1 is a 4K set.
findings.source_title: BK-102A Overview and Use Cases – OREI
findings.note: From the search summary of OREI's support articles. I did not open this page myself, so treat it as background and not a pick-deciding fact.
